Equipment: yoga mat and door pull‑up bar only. Goal: maintain strength and muscle mass (no hypertrophy progression), maintain movement quality, and manage recovery/nutrition so she returns ready to resume progressive overload.

Plan overview
- Duration: 2 weeks (14 days). Training 4 sessions/week: 3 resistance sessions + 1 mobility/active recovery session. Two rest days per week. This frequency preserves neuromuscular stimulus while allowing recovery during travel.
- Session focus: full‑body stimulus each resistance workout with emphasis on tempo, time under tension (TUT), and near‑maximal sets in the 6–12 rep range where possible. Use RPE 7–8 (stops 1–2 reps short of failure). Include unilateral work and hamstring/hip hinging variations to protect posterior chain.
- Progression model: no progressive overload required; simply hold load by matching efforts across days. Slight autoregulated increases (1–2 reps) allowed if feeling strong, but avoid pushing past RPE 8.
- Conditioning: short, low‑impact cardio (10–20 minutes) after sessions or on active day if desired. Avoid long high‑intensity sessions that would compromise recovery.
- Nutrition: maintain calorie at maintenance, protein 1.8–2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day, distribute protein across meals (~20–35 g each). Keep hydration and sleep 7–9 hours. If weight tends to fluctuate on travel, aim for slight caloric deficit no larger than 200 kcal if weight control is necessary, but for holding muscle aim to match maintenance.
- Recovery: emphasize sleep, mobility, daily walks, foam rolling if possible. Prioritize pre/post‑workout protein and gentle stretching.

Weekly schedule (repeat for Week 2 with minor variations listed)
- Day 1: Resistance A (Full‑body emphasis: vertical pull + horizontal push + squat + posterior chain unilateral)
- Day 2: Active Recovery / Mobility + optional low‑intensity cardio
- Day 3: Resistance B (Full‑body emphasis: vertical push + horizontal pull + hinge + single‑leg)
- Day 4: Rest or walking/light movement
- Day 5: Resistance C (Full‑body: mixed strength & metabolic maintenance — heavier-ish sets + higher TUT sets)
- Day 6: Rest
- Day 7: Optional mobility + easy walk or light cardio (keep it restorative)

Session structure and pacing
- Warm‑up (6–8 min): joint mobility, dynamic movements, 2 light sets of main movement patterns (e.g., assisted pull‑up negatives or scap pull aparts).
- Main work: 3–4 main exercises per resistance session. 2–3 working sets each at RPE 7–8. Reps generally 6–12 for strength/hypertrophy maintenance and 10–15 for accessory/TUT work.
- Tempo: use controlled tempo where helpful: eccentrics 2–4s, pause 0–1s, concentric explosive but controlled.
- Cooldown: 5–8 min stretching focusing on worked muscles.

Exercise list using only mat + door pull‑up bar (options/variations included)
- Pull‑up variations: full pull‑ups, assisted pull‑ups (feet on floor or band if available—use toe support), slow negatives (3–5s), isometric holds at top/mid.

- Push‑ups: standard, incline (hands on bed/desk), decline (feet elevated), slow eccentrics, narrow/diamond.

Legend / rules (applies both weeks)
- Equipment: yoga mat + door pull‑up bar only. Bodyweight-only.
- Intensity: Week 1 main sets RPE ~7–8; Week 2 main sets RPE ~7.5–8.5. Stop ~1–2 reps shy of failure.
- Sets: most main exercises = 3 working sets (unless noted). Reps generally 6–12; accessories 10–15.
- Tempo: use slow eccentrics (2–4s) and pauses where suggested.
- Cardio finisher: 15 minutes after resistance work. Options: stair intervals, hallway brisk run/walk, bodyweight EMOM, interval calisthenics ladder, or Tabata (low‑impact preferred).
- Nutrition: maintain calories at maintenance; protein 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day; hydrate; prioritize sleep.
- Tracking: weekly metric = weekly hard‑rep total for pull/push/single‑leg (target ~Week1 baseline; Week 2 +5–10%) + session adherence (3–4 sessions).

WEEK 1 (Maintenance; lower volume/intensity)
Day 1 — Resistance A
- Main: Assisted/full pull‑ups 3 x 6–10; Push‑ups 3 x 8–12 (3s down); Bulgarian split squats 3 x 8–10/leg; Single‑leg RDL (balance) 3 x 8–10/leg.
